threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success criteria, and responsibilities for the framework project.

messages.text:
Kicking off the Design and Rollout of Inclusive Hiring and Onboarding Framework project.
Goal: have a standardized, inclusive hiring and onboarding approach that we can run across all business units within 30 days, using our current HRIS.
Proposed scope:
- Map current hiring and onboarding flows and consolidate into a single process map (linked later as the main reference doc, similar to A1)
- Standard job posting and interview toolkit
- Inclusive hiring and anti-bias guideline
- Onboarding checklist and 90-day integration plan
- KPI definition and reporting approach
Out of scope for now:
- Any new HR tech implementation
- Changes to compensation philosophy or grading
For ownership, I suggest we follow the backlog: managers lead T1, T3, T5, T6, T8, T10, T12; assistants lead T2, T4, T7, T9, T11.
Can you all confirm if this scope and split works, or flag anything missing before we lock it in under D1 and D2

Thanks for framing this.
From my side, the scope looks reasonable and matches the backlog.
On ownership, I am happy to take point on T2, T4, T7, T9, and T11 on the assistant side, and coordinate with the other assistants so we do not duplicate work.
One question before we close D1 and D2: for the process map that will become A1, do we want to include detailed regional variations, or keep it at a global standard with notes where local labour rules differ
I ask because this will affect how we document T1 and how much input we need from legal and payroll.

Good point on regional differences.
Given the labour legislation constraints, I would suggest we keep A1 as a single global map but mark the steps where local rules may change, for example notice periods, medical checks, or contract formats.
For T1, I can collect the main legal and employment law variations we already know and add them as annotations, instead of separate flows.
On scope, I am aligned with what was proposed, but I am not sure if we should also mention disability accommodations explicitly in the scope, or if that is already covered under inclusive hiring.
What do you think

I am aligned with the overall scope and the split by tasks.
For T5 and T6, I can support on the payroll and KPI side, especially where we need to make sure we do not add manual steps.
One clarification: for the HR metrics sheet that will become A5 later, do we want to include only hiring and onboarding KPIs, or also some diversity indicators linked to inclusive hiring
This will influence how we define T6 and how we use the data from the pilot.

From the assistant side, I am ok with the scope and the ownership proposal.
I can support 167595 on T2 and T4, especially around inclusive language and making sure the onboarding checklist is easy for managers to follow.
I would just add that we explicitly call out support for people with disabilities and gender equality in the scope, so it does not get lost when we are under time pressure.

Agree with the proposed scope and task split.
I can back up on T7, T9, and T11, especially drafting FAQs and collecting feedback from employees and candidates.
No extra items from my side, but I support the idea of making disability and gender equality explicit in the scope statement.

On the process map question: I like the idea of a single global A1 with annotations for regional specifics.
That keeps T1 manageable and still lets us respect local labour rules.
For disability and gender equality, I agree we should make them explicit in the scope, not only in the guidelines.
On KPIs, I suggest we include a small set of diversity-related indicators in A5, but only where we already have data in HRIS, so we stay within the constraint of no new tools.
If there are no objections, I will update the scope statement accordingly before we mark D1 as agreed.

No objections from me.
For T1, I will work with 17956 to capture the main steps and pain points from the current flows, and we can add the regional notes you mentioned.
On KPIs for T6, I can draft an initial list that includes time to hire, offer acceptance, 90 day retention, and a couple of diversity indicators, and then we refine together.
From my side, we can close D1 with the updated scope you described.

I am aligned as well.
I will support T1 and T3, and also help check that the process map and guidelines reflect employment law basics.
No further changes to scope from my side, so ok to consider D1 closed.

Fine by me.
I will take T5 and T6 as proposed and coordinate with payroll to make sure we do not create extra manual work.
From my side, D1 and D2 can be confirmed.

All good with the updated scope and the task ownership.
Happy to support on the assistant tasks as discussed.
Ok to close D1 and D2.

Same here, no concerns.
The split between managers and assistants on the backlog looks clear enough for me.
Ready to move ahead with D1 and D2 confirmed.

Summarizing before we move on:
- Scope confirmed: process map (A1), toolkit, inclusive guideline, onboarding checklist and 90 day plan, and KPI definition (T6), all within current HRIS and legal constraints, with explicit focus on disability and gender equality.
- Out of scope: new HR tech and changes to compensation structure.
- Ownership: managers on T1, T3, T5, T6, T8, T10, T12; assistants on T2, T4, T7, T9, T11, with 167595 coordinating assistant work.
Based on the confirmations above, I am marking D1 and D2 as agreed so we can start execution.

Thanks for the recap.
I will start by drafting the current state inputs for T1 and aligning with assistants on T2 and T4 so that we keep the flow from process map to templates consistent.
Will share a first view of A1 and the related pieces in the next couple of days.

I will block time to review the early draft of A1 and make sure the main legal and employment law checkpoints are visible in the process.
Once we have that, it will be easier to move into T3 and T5 without missing key steps.

I will start sketching the HRIS and payroll touchpoints for T5 based on our current flows, so that when A1 is ready we can plug it in and check for gaps.
For T6, I will wait for the initial KPI list from 167595 and then we can refine together.

I will prepare some examples of inclusive language and accessibility notes that we can reuse in T2 and T4, so that the toolkit and onboarding checklist already reflect the inclusive focus from day one.
I will start a simple tracker for the backlog tasks so we can monitor progress against the 30 day deadline and keep an eye on dependencies between T1, T2, T4, and T6.

threads.thread_goal: Define and validate standardized hiring templates and inclusive guidelines.

messages.text:
Sharing the first draft of the job posting and interview toolkit for review.
This will become A4 and is linked to T2.
Key elements:
- Job posting template with sections for role summary, responsibilities, requirements, and a standard inclusion statement, plus notes on inclusive language.
- Structured interview guide with core behavioural questions and prompts to explore accommodations where relevant.
- Simple scorecard with clear criteria to reduce bias.
I drafted it to align with the early view of A1 so that the steps from requisition to offer are consistent.
I would like feedback on:
1) Clarity for non HR managers.
2) Any legal or employment law red flags.
3) Anything missing from an inclusion perspective before we move to pilot approval under D3.
Also, 17956, I know you are working on T3 and A2; it would be good to check that the toolkit and the guideline use the same concepts.

Thanks for sending this.
I had a first look at the job posting template and the interview guide.
From a legal and employment law angle, I did not see any obvious issues, but I want to double check the wording around disability and medical questions, to make sure we do not ask for information that is not allowed.
For A2 and T3, I have a rough outline of the inclusive hiring and anti bias guideline, but it is not fully written yet.
Maybe we can align on the structure first so that A4 and A2 match.
Could you share which sections you think should be mandatory for managers to read before they start interviewing

I went through the draft of A4.
Overall it reads clearly for managers, especially the scorecard.
A couple of suggestions:
- In the job posting template, we might want to add a short example of inclusive requirements, for instance avoiding unnecessary degree requirements.
- In the interview guide, we could add a short reminder about structured note taking to support fair decisions.
On D3, I think we should incorporate these small tweaks and then run a quick test with one or two managers before we say it is ready for pilot.
For A2 and T3, I suggest we keep the guideline concise, with practical examples of compliant and non compliant practices, so managers actually use it.

I focused on the inclusive language part.
The template already avoids most biased terms, but I suggest we add a short checklist for managers, for example avoid gendered language, avoid age references, and focus on skills.
We can also include a standard paragraph about accommodations for candidates with disabilities, so managers do not have to improvise.
This would tie nicely into A2 and T3.

I checked the interview guide from a practical point of view.
The flow is easy to follow, but I wonder if we should add a short section on how to open and close the interview, since some managers are not used to structured interviews.
Also, maybe we can add a note reminding them not to ask about family plans or similar topics, which often come up informally.

From my side, I checked if anything in A4 would create extra admin work.
It looks fine, as long as we keep the scorecard simple enough to be captured in our current HRIS.
For that reason, I would avoid too many free text fields and focus on a few clear criteria.
No blockers from me for D3 once the small edits are in.

Thanks for the feedback so far.
On the sections that should be mandatory for managers before interviewing, I suggest we align A2 around:
- Basic principles of inclusive hiring and bias awareness.
- Examples of what to ask and what not to ask, including disability and family topics.
- How to use the structured interview guide and scorecard from A4.
If you agree, I can adjust A4 to reference these sections explicitly, so managers see the link between the toolkit and the guideline.

That structure works for me.
For A2 under T3, I will draft three main parts:
1) Bias awareness and examples of unfair practices.
2) Disability accommodations and how to handle requests.
3) Do and do not lists for interview questions, aligned with the interview guide in A4.
I will also add a short section on gender equality in hiring decisions.
Once I have a draft, I will ask for a quick legal review from our external contact before we sign off under D4.

Good point on the HRIS.
Let us keep the scorecard to a small number of criteria with a simple rating scale and one free text field for key notes.
That should be easy to capture without new tools.
If everyone is ok, I suggest 167595 incorporates the edits from this thread into A4, and 17956 finalizes the first draft of A2.
Then we can do a quick round of comments and move to decisions D3 and D4.

I have now updated A4 with:
- Inclusive language checklist and standard accommodations paragraph.
- Opening and closing script suggestions.
- Clear link to the guideline sections you plan for A2.
I also simplified the scorecard fields so they can be captured in our current HRIS.
Unless there are strong objections, I think A4 is ready to be used in the pilot, so we can mark D3 as approved.

I reviewed the updated A4 and the inclusive language checklist looks good.
The accommodations paragraph is clear and should help managers feel more confident.
No further comments from me, so I support closing D3.

Same here, the interview flow feels more complete now with the opening and closing suggestions.
I think managers will appreciate the concrete examples.
Ok to move ahead with A4 for the pilot.

I have completed the first full draft of A2 under T3, following the structure we discussed.
It includes examples of compliant and non compliant questions, guidance on disability accommodations, and a short section on gender equality.
I will now send it to our external legal contact for a quick compliance check.
Assuming no major changes, we should be able to sign off on D4 shortly.

I skimmed A2 and it is very practical.
The do and do not lists are especially helpful.
From my side, I do not see anything that would conflict with our current HR processes.
Once you get the external legal confirmation, I am comfortable marking D4 as approved.

Great.
Please let us know once the external legal contact confirms there are no issues.
If the feedback is minor, we can incorporate it and still keep the guideline concise.
After that, I propose we formally record D4 as signed off and include A2 and A4 in the pilot package.

Update on the legal review: our external contact confirmed that the content of A2 is compliant, with only a couple of wording tweaks, which I have already applied.
With that, I consider A2 ready for use together with A4 in the pilot.
I am marking D4 as signed off.

Perfect.
With D3 and D4 closed, I will prepare a short one pager summarizing how managers should use A2 and A4 together during the pilot, so we keep the experience consistent.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize onboarding checklist, 90-day plan, and integration with payroll/HRIS.

messages.text:
I am sharing the draft onboarding checklist and 90 day integration plan, which will become A3 and is linked to T4.
Structure:
- Pre boarding: contracts, equipment, system access, and welcome communication.
- First week: orientation, manager check ins, basic training, and introductions.
- First month: role specific training, feedback touchpoint, and inclusion check.
- 90 days: performance and integration review, plus feedback from the new hire.
I tried to align the steps with the process map in A1 and kept the checklist simple enough for managers.
I would like feedback on:
1) Feasibility from a payroll and HRIS perspective (T5).
2) Whether we are covering people with disabilities and remote hires clearly enough.
3) Any steps that feel too heavy for managers.
Once we refine this, we can move toward D5 and D6.

Thanks for the draft.
From a payroll and HRIS angle, most steps look fine.
A couple of points for T5:
- For pre boarding, we should make sure the contract creation and HRIS entry happen before equipment ordering, otherwise we risk delays.
- For 90 day reviews, we should confirm whether we track this in HRIS or via a simple form, to avoid adding manual follow up.
If we keep the checklist aligned with existing fields, D6 should be straightforward.

Looking at A3 from a legal and compliance perspective, I do not see major issues.
We just need to ensure that any mandatory documents or medical checks required by local labour legislation are captured in the pre boarding section, maybe as a note that can vary by region.
For people with disabilities, we might want to add a step to confirm accommodations before day one and to review them during the first month.
That would also connect well with the inclusive hiring guideline in A2.

I checked the checklist with a focus on manager usability.
The structure is clear, but I suggest we:
- Add a short summary at the top with the key actions for each phase.
- Include a simple reminder for managers to introduce the new hire to any disability support resources we have.
For remote hires, maybe we can add a note about virtual introductions and equipment shipping timelines.

From a practical side, I think managers will appreciate checkboxes and short descriptions rather than long text.
Maybe we can also add a line for a 30 day check in, not only at 90 days, so issues are caught earlier.
Otherwise, the flow looks manageable.

I like the overall structure of A3.
To keep it lean and avoid the risk of low adoption, I would:
- Highlight which steps are mandatory versus recommended.
- Make sure the pre boarding steps are as automated as possible through HRIS and payroll, in line with T5.
If we can confirm with 441030 that the sequence works with current systems, we should be close to D5 and D6.

Thanks for the inputs.
I will adjust A3 to:
- Make contract creation and HRIS entry explicit before equipment ordering.
- Add a note that 90 day reviews can be tracked either in HRIS where available or via a simple form, to avoid blocking rollout.
I will also incorporate the suggestions on disability accommodations, remote hires, and mandatory versus recommended steps.
Once updated, I will share a short summary so we can decide on D5 and D6.

That sounds good.
For T5, I will map the exact touchpoints between A3 and our HRIS and payroll processes, especially for contract creation, start date, and first payroll run.
If I see any step that would add manual work, I will propose an alternative.
Assuming no major issues, I will confirm that the checklist is feasible from our side so we can close D6.

I will add a short note in A3 referencing A2 for managers who want more detail on inclusive practices during onboarding, especially around accommodations and gender equality.
This way, the checklist stays short but still points to the guideline for more context.

I have now updated A3 based on all comments:
- Clear sequence for pre boarding with contract and HRIS entry first.
- Explicit steps for accommodations and disability support, including a review during the first month.
- Notes for remote hires and virtual introductions.
- Mandatory versus recommended steps marked.
- References to A2 for more detail.
From my side, this version is ready for pilot use, so I propose we mark D5 as approved if there are no further concerns.

I completed the T5 review.
The updated A3 fits with our current HRIS and payroll processes.
We will not need new tools, and the only manual step is the 90 day review form where HRIS tracking is not available, which is acceptable.
With that, I am comfortable confirming that the payroll and HRIS touchpoints are aligned, and we can close D6.

Great work.
With D5 and D6 confirmed, we can include A3 in the pilot package alongside A1, A2, and A4.
Next step will be to reflect this in the manager training materials under T7.
I will take the updated A3 and start drafting a simple manager facing version for the training pack, so that the checklist feels less like a form and more like a practical guide.

I can help test the checklist with one or two recent onboarding cases to see if any steps are unclear before the pilot starts.
I will share any findings in the next check in.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and monitor the pilot, including training and communication to managers.

messages.text:
Now that A2, A3, and A4 are in good shape, we need to plan the pilot.
Proposal for D7:
- Pilot business unit: Customer Operations, as they have a steady volume of hiring and a mix of on site and remote roles.
- Timeframe: next 4 weeks, within our overall 30 day project window.
Scope for the pilot under T8:
- At least three roles hired using the new process.
- Use of A1, A2, A3, and A4 end to end.
For D8 and T7, we also need to approve the manager communication and training plan.
Initial idea:
- Short virtual training session (45 minutes) for Customer Operations managers.
- Manager Communication and Training Pack (A6) with a quick reference guide and FAQ.
Please share any concerns with the proposed business unit and dates, or alternative suggestions, before we lock in D7 and D8.

Customer Operations sounds like a good choice for the pilot, since they have enough volume to test the framework properly.
Only concern is that they sometimes have urgent hires, so we should be careful that the new process does not slow them down too much.
Maybe we can agree with their manager on which roles will go through the pilot and which can follow the old process if there is an emergency.
On the training, a 45 minute session seems reasonable, as long as the materials in A6 are very clear and not too long.

I support using Customer Operations for the pilot.
From a payroll and HRIS perspective, they are already used to structured processes, so it should be manageable.
We just need to make sure the managers understand that the new steps do not change how they submit data to payroll.
For T7, I suggest we include one slide in A6 that shows clearly what stays the same and what changes for them.

I agree that Customer Operations is a good pilot area.
For T7, I can draft the training deck and quick reference guide for A6, focusing on:
- How to use A2, A3, and A4 in practice.
- What is mandatory versus recommended.
- How to escalate issues using T11 once it is ready.
On timing, if we confirm D7 and D8 this week, we can schedule two training sessions next week to cover different time zones.

I can help with the FAQ section for A6 under T7.
Based on past questions from managers, I will include topics like:
- How to handle candidates who request accommodations.
- What to do if they are short on time but still need to follow the new steps.
- Who to contact if they are unsure about a legal or payroll question.
This should support both D7 and D8 by making the pilot smoother.

From my side, no objections to Customer Operations or the 4 week timeframe.
I suggest we also plan how we will collect feedback during the pilot under T9, so that managers know from the start that we will ask for their input.
We can mention this in the training and in A6.

Good call on urgent hires.
When we speak with the Customer Operations manager, we can agree that:
- At least three roles will go fully through the new framework.
- In case of urgent backfills, they can use the old process, but we encourage them to try at least the new templates.
I will set up a short call with the business unit manager to confirm this and the 4 week window.
If they agree, we can mark D7 as confirmed.

On T9, I can prepare a short feedback survey and an interview script for managers and candidates.
We can introduce this during the training so they know what to expect.
The results will later feed into A7, the Pilot Feedback Summary Report.

Once you have the confirmation from the Customer Operations manager, please share the agreed roles and dates here.
I will then make sure payroll and HRIS are aware of the pilot so they are not surprised by any new templates coming through.

Update: I spoke with the Customer Operations manager.
They agreed to participate in the pilot for the next 4 weeks and suggested three roles that will definitely go through the new framework.
They are also open to using the new templates for additional roles if time allows.
Based on this, I am marking D7 as agreed: Customer Operations as the pilot unit, with a 4 week timeframe and at least three roles using the full process.

Great.
I will finalize the training deck and quick reference guide for A6 under T7, incorporating:
- Overview of the new framework.
- How to use A2, A3, and A4.
- What stays the same for payroll and HRIS.
- How feedback will be collected under T9.
Once the materials are ready, we can schedule the two training sessions and then mark D8 as approved.

I have drafted the FAQ section for A6 and added the questions we discussed.
I will share it with you so you can integrate it into the training pack.
After that, I think the communication and training plan will be clear enough for managers.

I can support by scheduling the two training sessions and sending calendar invites to the Customer Operations managers, including the A6 pack as a pre read.
I will also track attendance so we know who might need a follow up.

Once the deck and FAQ are integrated into A6 and the two training sessions are scheduled, I am comfortable saying that the manager communication and training plan is ready for the pilot.
Please confirm here when that is done so we can formally mark D8 as approved.

Quick update: A6 is now complete with the deck, quick reference guide, and FAQ, and 552174 has scheduled the two training sessions with Customer Operations managers.
Given this, I propose we mark D8 as approved so we can start the pilot as planned.

Confirmed from my side.
I have informed payroll and HRIS about the pilot and shared the key slides from A6 that explain what changes for them.
Ready to support once the first pilot roles start.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot feedback, agree on adjustments, and confirm final rollout plan.

messages.text:
We have completed the pilot with Customer Operations and I am sharing the Pilot Feedback Summary Report, which is A7, under T9 and T10.
Key findings:
- Candidates appreciated the structured interviews and clear communication.
- Some managers felt the onboarding checklist A3 was a bit long, but they liked the mandatory versus recommended split.
- Time to hire did not increase significantly, but managers asked for clearer guidance on when they can skip optional steps.
- A few accessibility issues were raised around virtual interviews and document formats.
I have also drafted a list of proposed changes to the framework for T10.
We now need to agree on which changes to adopt (D9) and then confirm the go live date and governance model under T12 (D10).

Thanks for pulling A7 together.
Could you summarize the main proposed changes from T10 here, especially anything that affects A1, A2, A3, or A4
That will help us decide on D9.
Also, do we have any early data for the KPIs we defined in T6, such as time to hire and 90 day retention, even if the sample is small

Sure, main proposed changes from T10 are:
- A1: add a short visual legend to highlight which steps are mandatory and which are optional.
- A2: include one more example on handling virtual interviews for candidates with disabilities.
- A3: slightly reduce the number of recommended steps in the first week and clarify which can be combined.
- A4: add a short reminder about sending interview questions in advance when reasonable accommodations are needed.
On KPIs from T6, we have early data for time to hire and offer acceptance, but 90 day retention will only be visible later.
Time to hire stayed within our usual range, and offer acceptance was slightly higher, though the sample is small.

From a legal and compliance angle, the proposed changes look safe.
The additions to A2 and A4 around virtual interviews and accommodations are positive and do not create new risks.
For A1 and A3, marking mandatory versus optional steps more clearly should help managers follow the process without confusion.
I support adopting these changes under D9.

I checked the impact of the proposed changes on payroll and HRIS.
The updates to A1 and A3 do not change the underlying data we need, they just clarify the flow.
The reminder in A4 about sending questions in advance is also fine from a systems point of view.
No objections from me to adopting these changes for D9.

From the manager feedback I saw, the main pain point was understanding which onboarding steps were optional.
The proposed simplification in A3 should address that.
I also like the idea of adding more concrete examples in A2 and A4 for virtual interviews and accommodations.
I support adopting the full list of changes for D9.

I agree with the proposed adjustments.
During the pilot, managers also asked for a clearer escalation path when they were unsure about exceptions.
Once T11 and A8 are finalized, we should make sure they are clearly referenced in the final framework and in the training materials.

Good point on escalation.
As part of T11, I have drafted A8, the Issue Escalation and Governance Checklist, with common issue types and owners.
We can link A8 from A1 and A6 so managers know where to look.
Given the feedback so far, I propose we adopt all the changes listed for A1, A2, A3, and A4, and integrate A8 into the package, and mark D9 as agreed.

I am aligned with adopting the full set of changes under D9.
Next we need to confirm D10: go live date and governance model under T12.
Proposal:
- Go live date: two weeks from now, to give us time to apply the agreed changes and update A6.
- Governance: 17956 as overall owner of the framework, with 167595 as operational contact for updates.
- Review cycle: formal review every 6 months, with a simple change log as per T12.
Please share any concerns or suggestions before we lock in D10.

I can take the overall ownership of the framework under T12, with 167595 as the operational contact.
A 6 month review cycle sounds reasonable, and we can always trigger an earlier review if there are major legal changes.
The go live date in two weeks gives us enough time to apply the changes from T10 and update the documents.
No objections from me to D10 as proposed.

From a payroll and HRIS side, a go live in two weeks is fine.
We just need to communicate the final version of the process map A1 and any changes that affect data entry.
I also suggest we include a short note in the governance document about how to involve payroll when changes are proposed.

I support the proposed go live date and governance model.
For the change log under T12, I can help set up a simple template so we track what changed, why, and when, including any impact on managers.

No concerns from my side.
Two weeks is enough to refresh A6 and communicate the final framework to managers.
I will also update any FAQs to reflect the new escalation path in A8.

Given the confirmations above, I am marking D10 as agreed with:
- Go live in two weeks.
- 17956 as framework owner, 167595 as operational contact.
- 6 month review cycle with a simple change log as per T12.
Next steps are to finalize the document updates under T10 and T12 and communicate the go live to all managers.

I will coordinate the final updates for T10, applying the agreed changes to A1, A2, A3, and A4, and ensure A7 and A8 are linked where relevant.
I will also prepare a short summary for managers highlighting what is new versus what stays the same.
I will finalize the governance document under T12, including ownership, review cycle, and the change log template, and share it for visibility before go live.
